### Short summary

*What are the challenges and opportunities that can emerge from an agriculture without chemical pesticides in Sweden ?*

The recent ban of several per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in Denmark shows how the availability of chemical pesticides will keep on declining in the nearest future.
However, how the shift towards alternative pest control strategies will affect crop yield and farm profitability is still largely uncertain.
In 2026, the Swedish Plant Protection Council commissioned a report on the potential impacts of a withdrawal of trifluoroacetate-forming compounds in insecticides, expressing the need for actionable knowledge to support the agroecological transition of Swedish cropping systems.

Our project aims 
(1) to identify which crops would be the most affected by a general ban of chemical pesticides and 
(2) to explore the benefits and trade-offs of current pest control alternatives.

To address our first objective, we will perform a vulnerability analysis of Swedish cropping systems to chemical pesticide withdrawal based on expert knowledge and pesticide trial data from the Nordic Field Trial System.
In a second phase, we will assess the potential of integrated pest control management strategies in most economically important crops and test their effects in two field studies.
The first field study will be conducted in 2027 and will investigate the efficiency of early-flowering cultivar mixture in limiting pest incidence in winter oilseed rape. 
In ten farmer fields distributed across Skåne, we will assess crop yield and damages caused by the cabbage stem flea beetle (*Psylliodes chrysocephala*), the pollen beetle (*Brassicogethes aeneus*), the blue stem weevil (*Ceutorhynchus sulcicollis*), the cabbage seed weevil (*Ceutorhynchus obstrictus*) and the brassica pod midge (*Dasineura brassicae*).
The second study will be conducted in 2028, and its focus will be determined by the outcome of the potentiality assessment.
